An Agent Skill is its machine-loadable counterpart: "a directory containing a SKILL.md file" with a name, description, body, and optional scripts, published as an open standard [[equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills-anthropic]].

The SOP's applicability clause becomes the `description`, which must say "both what the Skill does and when to use it" [[agent-skills-claude-platform-docs]]; deterministic steps become scripts, which make a workflow "consistent and repeatable" [[equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills-anthropic]]; judgment steps become the body; the definition of done becomes a machine-checkable assertion; and the escalation clause becomes a reversibility tag the dispatcher gates on.

The largest study of Skill revisions, covering 3,159 Skills across 21 models, yields three authoring rules [[agent-skill-evolution-how-revisions-affect-coding-agents]]: name the command, path, or identifier (+0.41 compliance across 16 models); never silently delete a load-bearing rule (removing one that had *replaced* an older rule cut compliance by 0.58, against 0.12 for a duplicate); and keep Skills small (an added rule's benefit fell from +0.424 at low context occupancy to +0.270 at three-quarters full).

The registry is therefore signed and versioned, every Skill ships with evals per the rule "Start with evaluation" [[equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills-anthropic]], and agents may *propose* revisions that only an eval-gated promotion merges.

**Prediction.** Agent traces use small alphabets of 6–42 activity symbols, and collapsing a trace corpus into a deterministic finite-state machine (FSM), a graph of states with probabilistic transitions, takes 1–110 ms with no hyperparameters [[automata-from-agent-traces]].

**Execution.** PASTE shows tool execution accounts for 60% of latency in coding tasks, and 55% of file-editor writes are immediately followed by a pytest or python call [[act-while-thinking-accelerating-llm-agents-via-pattern-aware-speculative-tool-ex]].

PASTE represents each pattern as a tuple (C, T, f, p), where f is a symbolic value-mapping function that binds arguments late, for example taking a visit URL from the preceding search's JSON output, which works because 95% of visit URLs are a strict substring of that output [[act-while-thinking-accelerating-llm-agents-via-pattern-aware-speculative-tool-ex]].

**The governance addition.** PASTE's own audit found 602 potentially side-effecting actions among more than 20,000 speculative ones, all of which had to be blocked [[act-while-thinking-accelerating-llm-agents-via-pattern-aware-speculative-tool-ex]]. **Inference:** a push, a paid API call, or a migration cannot be cleanly aborted, so speculation splits on each Skill's reversibility tag.

The FSM also works as a brake: its anomaly features predict failure with held-out AUROC up to 0.941, supporting an early stop at 32% of trace completion that saves 68% of the remaining compute [[automata-from-agent-traces]].

AI-assisted analysis cut analysis time by 70–85%, found 15–30% more integration points than manual work, and kept false positives below 5%, but only "with human validation" [[ai-reverse-engineering-of-legacy-platforms-dynamics-consulting]].

**The steel-man is serious.** Continuous testing should fire "when material risk changes, not when the calendar dictates," and agents already run reconnaissance and exploit chaining unsupervised [[automated-penetration-testing-full-autonomy-fell-to-9]].
Across 431 OSS-Fuzz projects, an agent using GPT-5 found 22 confirmed zero-days [[cybergym-evaluating-ai-agents-real-world-cybersecurity-capabilities-at-scale]].

On ExploitGym's 898 real vulnerabilities, Claude Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5 produced working exploits for 157 and 120 within a two-hour limit (with safeguards disabled), and some succeeded even with ASLR and sandboxes enabled [[exploitgym-can-ai-agents-turn-security]].

OpenAI tells defenders to prepare for "AI-enabled attackers that work faster, at a larger scale" [[the-hugging-face-incident-and-the-road-ahead-openai]], and Google's threat intelligence group reports adversaries moving toward highly autonomous tooling [[gtig-ai-threat-tracker-from-prompting-to-autonomy-the-evolution-of-adversarial-a]].

And the frameworks object to missing *attribution*, not to cadence, so logging and audit trails could satisfy them without live human gating each cycle; APTS Tier 1 is already designed for low-friction, non-production operation [[owasp-apts-autonomous-penetration-testing-standard-owasp-foundation]].

1. **The industry retreated from full autonomy after trying it.** Full reliance on autonomous pentesting fell from 29% to 9% among 455 security leaders, with 47% moving to hybrid approaches [[automated-penetration-testing-full-autonomy-fell-to-9]], driven by 78% of teams reporting *critical false negatives* [[the-ai-pentesting-pulse-decoding-the-27x-risk-multiplier-in-llm-deployments]].

Both figures come from a vendor of human-led testing, but the independent CREST snapshot points the same way: 9% use autonomous agent-based testing, against 47% for AI-assisted reporting and 44% for scanning [[automated-penetration-testing-full-autonomy-fell-to-9]].

2. **Regulation attaches accountability for testing and evidence to persons.** PCI DSS 11.4 requires an independent tester, DORA Article 27 indemnity insurance, and NCSC CHECK cleared individuals; SOC 2 CC4.1 accepts agent-produced evidence only "provided a named human signs it" [[automated-penetration-testing-full-autonomy-fell-to-9]].

3. **The most motivated actor kept humans in the loop.** A state-sponsored group automated 80–90% of an espionage campaign across about 30 targets yet still needed humans at 4–6 decision points, because the model fabricated credentials, overstated findings, and misflagged public information as critical discoveries [[disrupting-an-ai-orchestrated-cyber-espionage-campaign-anthropic]].

The checkpoints mark a 2025 hallucination limit, not a durable ceiling, and adversary autonomy is rising [[gtig-ai-threat-tracker-from-prompting-to-autonomy-the-evolution-of-adversarial-a]], which is why the cadence stays machine-speed while only production promotion waits.

4. **The most mature fix loop stops at a pull request.** GitHub's agentic autofix generates a fix, re-verifies it with CodeQL in 2–4 minutes, and always opens a PR [[agentic-autofix-for-code-scanning-alerts-in-public-preview-github-changelog]].

Anthropic advises using frameworks only if "you understand the underlying code," because abstractions "obscure the underlying prompts and responses" [[building-effective-ai-agents-anthropic]], so a factory whose safety depends on inspectability defaults to a thin custom Director whose fan-out is code.

Where a framework is wanted, LangGraph is rated "most production-ready" for stateful workflows [[langgraph-vs-autogen-vs-crewai-an-agent-framework-comparison]], is the "only option that cleanly handles routing between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google models" [[openai-agents-sdk-vs-langgraph-vs-autogen-building-production-agents-openhelm]], and lets ledger checks run as graph nodes, whereas migrating off CrewAI later means "a rewrite rather than a port" [[langgraph-vs-autogen-vs-crewai-an-agent-framework-comparison]].
